item.title: Agar Cube Diffusion and Surface Area-to-Volume Ratio
item.stimulus:
Students model cells using cubes of agar that contain a pH indicator. The indicator changes color wherever acid has diffused into the agar. Three cubes with side lengths of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm were fully submerged in the same dilute acid solution at the same temperature for 10 minutes. Each cube was then removed, blotted, and cut in half. In every cube, the acid had diffused inward to a depth of 0.3 cm from every face. This left an inner cube of unchanged color with a side length 0.6 cm shorter than the original cube.

Useful relationships for a cube with side length s: surface area SA = 6s² and volume V = s³. For a sphere with radius r: SA = 4πr² and V = (4/3)πr³.

Table 1. Results after 10 minutes in acid
Cube side length (cm) | SA:V ratio (cm⁻¹) | Depth of acid penetration (cm) | Side length of unchanged inner cube (cm) | Percent of cube volume reached by acid
1 | 6.0 | 0.3 | 0.4 | 93.6%
2 | ? | 0.3 | 1.4 | 65.7%
3 | 2.0 | 0.3 | 2.4 | ?
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6s² = 6(2 cm)² = 24 cm². V = s³ = (2 cm)³ = 8 cm³. SA:V = 24 cm² / 8 cm³ = 3 cm⁻¹.

(b) Total volume = (3 cm)³ = 27 cm³. Unchanged inner volume = (2.4 cm)³ = 13.824 cm³. Volume reached by acid = 27 − 13.824 = 13.176 cm³. Percent = 13.176 / 27 × 100 = 48.8%.

(c) As the SA:V ratio decreases, the percent of the cube's volume reached by the acid also decreases. The 1 cm cube (SA:V 6.0 cm⁻¹) was 93.6% penetrated. The 2 cm cube (3 cm⁻¹) was 65.7% penetrated. The 3 cm cube (2.0 cm⁻¹) was only 48.8% penetrated.

(d) The SA:V ratio will be cut in half. For a sphere, SA:V = 4πr² / ((4/3)πr³) = 3/r. At r = 5 µm, SA:V = 3/5 = 0.6 µm⁻¹. At r = 10 µm, SA:V = 3/10 = 0.3 µm⁻¹. This happens because surface area increases 4 times while volume increases 8 times. The larger cell has much more cytoplasm that needs nutrients and oxygen and produces waste. However, it has relatively less plasma membrane per unit of volume through which these materials can move. Exchange with the environment therefore becomes less efficient, and the cell may not be able to obtain resources or remove wastes fast enough to meet its needs.

# part a
s=2
SA=6*s**2; V=s**3
assert SA==24 and V==8 and SA/V==3
# table SA:V values
assert 6*1**2/1**3==6 and abs(6*3**2/3**3-2.0)<1e-12
# percent reached for each cube, depth 0.3 cm
def pct(s):
    inner=s-0.6
    return (1-(inner/s)**3)*100
assert abs((1-0.6)-0.4)<1e-12 and abs((2-0.6)-1.4)<1e-12 and abs((3-0.6)-2.4)<1e-12
assert abs(pct(1)-93.6)<0.05
assert abs(pct(2)-65.7)<0.05
assert abs(pct(3)-48.8)<0.05
# part b details
assert abs(2.4**3-13.824)<1e-9
assert abs(27-2.4**3-13.176)<1e-9
assert abs(13.176/27*100-48.8)<0.05
# part d
def sav(r):
    return (4*math.pi*r**2)/((4/3)*math.pi*r**3)
assert abs(sav(5)-0.6)<1e-12 and abs(sav(10)-0.3)<1e-12
assert abs((4*math.pi*10**2)/(4*math.pi*5**2)-4)<1e-12
assert abs(((4/3)*math.pi*10**3)/((4/3)*math.pi*5**3)-8)<1e-12
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Agar Cube Diffusion and Surface Area-to-Volume Ratio
item.stimulus:
Students model cells using cubes of agar that contain phenolphthalein, an indicator that turns pink when sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is present. They cut cubes with side lengths of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 4 cm and soak all three cubes in the same NaOH solution for 10 minutes. They then rinse the cubes, cut them in half, and find that NaOH reached a depth of 0.4 cm from every face in every cube. From this depth they calculate the percent of each cube's volume that turned pink. The relevant equations are: surface area of a cube SA = 6s² and volume of a cube V = s³, where s is the length of one side.

Cube side (cm) | SA:V ratio (cm⁻¹) | Percent of volume turned pink
1 | 6.0 | 99.2
2 | 3.0 | 78.4
4 | ? | 48.8
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6s² = 6(4 cm)² = 96 cm². V = s³ = (4 cm)³ = 64 cm³. SA:V = 96/64 = 1.5 cm⁻¹.

(b) As the SA:V ratio decreases, the percent of the cube's volume that turned pink decreases. The 1 cm cube (SA:V 6.0 cm⁻¹) was 99.2% pink, while the 4 cm cube (SA:V 1.5 cm⁻¹) was only 48.8% pink.

(c) When a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area (volume scales with s³, surface area with s²), so the SA:V ratio falls. The demand for nutrients and the production of wastes depend on the volume, but exchange can occur only across the membrane surface. In a very large cell, the membrane could not supply enough materials or remove wastes fast enough for the whole volume, just as NaOH failed to reach about half of the 4 cm cube in 10 minutes.

(d) The folded cube will have a greater percent of its volume turn pink than the 48.8% of the unfolded 4 cm cube. The folds increase surface area without changing volume, so the SA:V ratio increases. More surface is available for NaOH to enter per unit of volume, and the interior is closer to a surface, so more of the volume is reached in the same time. This is why cells such as gut epithelial cells have membrane folds.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction as F
d=F(4,10)
def ratio(s): return F(6*s*s, s**3)
def pink(s):
    inner=s-2*d
    return (1-(inner/s)**3)*100
assert ratio(1)==6 and ratio(2)==3 and ratio(4)==F(3,2)
assert 6*4**2==96 and 4**3==64
assert abs(float(pink(1))-99.2)<1e-9
assert abs(float(pink(2))-78.4)<1e-9
assert abs(float(pink(4))-48.8)<1e-9
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Agar Cube Size, SA:V, and Diffusion Efficiency
item.stimulus:
Students modeled cells using agar blocks containing phenolphthalein. Phenolphthalein is colorless but turns pink wherever sodium hydroxide (NaOH) has diffused into the agar. They cut cubes with side lengths of 1 cm, 2 cm and 3 cm. They placed each cube in NaOH solution for 10 minutes, then removed and sliced it. In every cube the pink layer had a uniform depth of 0.30 cm on all faces. The colorless, unpenetrated core of each cube is therefore a cube with side length (s − 0.60 cm), where s is the cube's side length.

Relevant equations: surface area of a cube, SA = 6s²; volume of a cube, V = s³; surface area of a rectangular solid, SA = 2lh + 2lw + 2wh; volume of a rectangular solid, V = lwh.

Side length (cm) | SA:V (cm⁻¹) | Depth of pink layer (cm) | Percent of volume pink
1 | 6.0 | 0.30 | 93.6
2 | ? | 0.30 | 65.7
3 | 2.0 | 0.30 | ?
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6s² = 6(2 cm)² = 24 cm². V = s³ = (2 cm)³ = 8 cm³. SA:V = 24/8 = 3.0 cm⁻¹.

(b) Total volume = 3³ = 27 cm³. The core has side 3 − 0.60 = 2.4 cm, so core volume = 2.4³ = 13.824 cm³. Pink volume = 27 − 13.824 = 13.176 cm³. Percent pink = 13.176/27 × 100 ≈ 48.8%.

(c) As the cubes get larger, SA:V drops from 6.0 to 3.0 to 2.0 cm⁻¹, and the percent of volume reached by NaOH drops from 93.6% to 65.7% to about 48.8%. Materials enter and leave a cell only across its plasma membrane (the surface), but the cell's demand for nutrients and its production of wastes depend on its volume. In a large cell there is too little membrane surface relative to volume, so exchange cannot keep up and inner regions are poorly supplied. Small cells have a high SA:V and exchange materials efficiently, so cells are typically small.

(d) The percent pink will be greater than in the 2 cm cube. The block has SA = 2(1)(8) + 2(1)(8) + 2(1)(1) = 34 cm² and V = 8 cm³, so SA:V = 4.25 cm⁻¹, higher than the cube's 3.0 cm⁻¹. With more surface per unit volume, and no point more than 0.5 cm from a surface, NaOH reaches a larger fraction of the volume. The core would be 0.4 × 0.4 × 7.4 = 1.184 cm³, so about (8 − 1.184)/8 × 100 ≈ 85.2% turns pink.
item.verification_python:
import math
d=0.30
def cube(s):
    sa=6*s**2; v=s**3; core=(s-2*d)**3
    return sa,v,sa/v,(v-core)/v*100
sa,v,r,p=cube(2)
assert sa==24 and v==8 and math.isclose(r,3.0)
assert abs(p-65.7)<0.05
sa1,v1,r1,p1=cube(1)
assert math.isclose(r1,6.0) and abs(p1-93.6)<0.05
sa3,v3,r3,p3=cube(3)
assert math.isclose(r3,2.0)
assert math.isclose((3-0.6)**3,13.824,abs_tol=1e-9)
assert math.isclose(27-13.824,13.176,abs_tol=1e-9)
assert abs(p3-48.8)<0.05
l,w,h=1,1,8
sab=2*l*h+2*l*w+2*w*h
vb=l*w*h
assert sab==34 and vb==8 and math.isclose(sab/vb,4.25)
core=(l-2*d)*(w-2*d)*(h-2*d)
assert math.isclose(core,1.184,abs_tol=1e-9)
pb=(vb-core)/vb*100
assert abs(pb-85.2)<0.05
assert pb>p
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Agar Cube Diffusion and Surface Area-to-Volume Ratio
item.stimulus:
Students model cells with cube-shaped blocks of agar that contain a pH indicator. The indicator turns pink where a basic solution has diffused into the agar. Three cubes with side lengths of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 4 cm are placed on a mesh support in a basic solution, so every face is exposed. After 10 minutes, the students cut each cube in half. In every cube, the solution has diffused 0.25 cm inward from each face. They then calculate the percentage of each cube's volume that turned pink.

Cube side length (cm) | Surface area-to-volume ratio (cm⁻¹) | Percent of volume colored pink
1 | 6.0 | 87.5
2 | 3.0 | 57.8
4 | ? | 33.0
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6s² = 6(4 cm)² = 96 cm². V = s³ = (4 cm)³ = 64 cm³. SA:V = 96/64 = 1.5 cm⁻¹.

(b) As the surface area-to-volume ratio decreases, the percent of volume colored pink decreases. The cube with SA:V 6.0 was 87.5% pink, while the cube with SA:V 1.5 was only 33.0% pink.

(c) When a cell's volume increases, its surface area increases more slowly, so its SA:V decreases. That leaves less plasma membrane per unit of volume through which nutrients enter and wastes leave, even though the larger volume demands more resources. In the model, diffusion travels the same distance (0.25 cm) in every cube. So in larger cubes a smaller fraction of the interior is reached in the same time, falling from 87.5% to 33.0%. A large cell would likewise be unable to supply its interior efficiently.

(d) The flat block will have a greater percent of its volume colored pink than the 4 cm cube; in fact, about 100%. Its surface area is 2(16×8) + 2(16×0.5) + 2(8×0.5) = 256 + 16 + 8 = 280 cm². Its SA:V is therefore 280/64 ≈ 4.4 cm⁻¹, much higher than the cube's 1.5 cm⁻¹. Also, the block is only 0.5 cm thick, so the 0.25 cm of diffusion from each face meets in the middle. That leaves no uncolored interior, compared with 67% uncolored in the cube.

item.title: Agar Cube Model of Cell Size and Diffusion
item.stimulus:
Students modeled cells using agar cubes that contain phenolphthalein, an indicator that turns pink when exposed to a base. They cut cubes with side lengths of 1 cm, 2 cm and 4 cm. They soaked all cubes in the same sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution for 10 minutes. They then cut each cube in half and measured how far the pink color had spread inward from each face. In every cube, NaOH had diffused 0.4 cm inward from every face. The unpenetrated center of each cube is a smaller cube whose side length equals the original side length minus 0.8 cm.

Side length (cm) | Surface area (cm²) | Volume (cm³) | SA:V (cm⁻¹) | Depth of diffusion (cm) | Percent of volume turned pink
1 | 6 | 1 | 6.0 | 0.4 | 99.2%
2 | 24 | 8 | ? | 0.4 | 78.4%
4 | 96 | 64 | 1.5 | 0.4 | ?
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6 × 2² = 24 cm². V = 2³ = 8 cm³. SA:V = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 cm⁻¹ (3:1).

(b) The unpenetrated center has side 4 − 0.8 = 3.2 cm, so its volume is 3.2³ = 32.768 cm³. Pink volume = 64 − 32.768 = 31.232 cm³. Percent pink = 31.232 ÷ 64 × 100 = 48.8%.

(c) As SA:V decreases, the percent of the volume reached by NaOH decreases: the 1 cm cube (SA:V 6.0 cm⁻¹) was 99.2% pink, the 2 cm cube (3 cm⁻¹) was 78.4% pink, and the 4 cm cube (1.5 cm⁻¹) was only 48.8% pink. As a cell gets larger, its volume increases with the cube of its side length while its surface area increases only with the square. A larger cell therefore has less plasma membrane per unit of volume through which to take in nutrients and remove wastes. More of its interior is far from the surface, so diffusion cannot supply the interior fast enough to meet its internal demand.

(d) The rectangular solid will have a greater percent of its volume turn pink than the 2 cm cube. Its SA = 2(1×2) + 2(1×4) + 2(2×4) = 28 cm², so SA:V = 28 ÷ 8 = 3.5 cm⁻¹, which is higher than 3 cm⁻¹ for the cube of the same volume. With more surface per unit of volume, and no point more than 0.5 cm from a surface, NaOH reaches more of the interior. Its unpenetrated core is 0.2 × 1.2 × 3.2 = 0.768 cm³, so about 90.4% turns pink, compared with 78.4% for the cube.

item.title: Agar Cube Size, Shape, and Diffusion Efficiency
item.stimulus:
Students modeled cells using cubes of agar that contain phenolphthalein, an indicator that turns pink when sodium hydroxide (NaOH) enters the agar. They cut cubes of three side lengths and soaked each cube in NaOH solution for 10 minutes. In every cube, the NaOH diffused 0.3 cm inward from each exposed face. The students then cut each cube open and calculated the percent of the cube's volume that had turned pink. For a cube, surface area SA = 6s² and volume V = s³, where s is the side length. For a rectangular solid, SA = 2lh + 2lw + 2wh and V = lwh.

Side length (cm) | SA (cm²) | V (cm³) | SA:V (cm⁻¹) | Percent of volume turned pink
1 | 6 | 1 | 6.0 | 93.6%
2 | 24 | 8 | 3.0 | 65.7%
3 | ? | ? | ? | 48.8%
item.model_answer:
(a) SA = 6s² = 6(3 cm)² = 54 cm². V = s³ = (3 cm)³ = 27 cm³. SA:V = 54/27 = 2 cm⁻¹ (2:1).

(b) As the surface area-to-volume ratio decreases, the percent of the cube's volume that turned pink also decreases. The 1 cm cube (SA:V = 6.0) was 93.6% pink, the 2 cm cube (SA:V = 3.0) was 65.7% pink, and the 3 cm cube (SA:V = 2.0) was only 48.8% pink.

(c) As a cell gets larger, its volume increases faster than its surface area, so its SA:V decreases. The volume determines how much material the cell needs and how much waste it produces, while the plasma membrane surface is where exchange happens. In a large cell, like the large agar cubes whose centers never turned pink, the membrane cannot exchange nutrients and wastes fast enough to supply the whole interior. Small cells have a high SA:V and exchange materials efficiently, so cell size is limited.

(d) The percent of the block that turns pink will be greater than 65.7%. The block's SA = 2(4)(1) + 2(4)(2) + 2(2)(1) = 8 + 16 + 4 = 28 cm², and V = 8 cm³, so SA:V = 28/8 = 3.5 cm⁻¹, which is higher than the cube's 3.0 cm⁻¹. With more surface area per unit of volume, and a thin 1 cm dimension so that no point is far from a surface, NaOH diffusing 0.3 cm inward reaches a larger fraction of the block (about 76%).

item.stimulus:

V = (4/3)π(2)³ = (32/3)π μm³.
SA/V = 16π ÷ (32π/3) = 48/32 = 1.5 μm⁻¹.

(b) For cell B, r = 6 μm: SA = 4π(6)² = 144π μm² and V = (4/3)π(6)³ = 288π μm³, so SA/V = 0.5 μm⁻¹.
1.5 μm⁻¹ ÷ 0.5 μm⁻¹ = 3, so cell A's surface area-to-volume ratio is 3 times that of cell B.

(c) Cell B's SA:V (0.5 μm⁻¹) is only one-third of cell A's (1.5 μm⁻¹). Materials are exchanged across the plasma membrane, so cell B has much less membrane surface for each unit of volume that needs nutrients and produces wastes. Exchange across the membrane therefore cannot keep up with the needs of B's volume as well as it can in A, so B is less efficient at exchanging materials.

(d) The shrew has the higher metabolic rate per unit body mass. Because it is much smaller, the shrew has a much higher surface area-to-volume ratio, so it exchanges heat with its environment proportionally faster and loses heat quickly for its mass. To keep its body temperature constant, it must produce more heat through metabolism per unit of body mass than the moose does.
